lacks.null-list: The harness stores aNumberList as adversarial_number_list_elements rows, a has_many association, so a null list and [] are both zero rows: a row sent to the PDP as null cannot be stored.

arithmetic/divide/field-by-field.reason: The denominator is a DIFFERENT column, so it may be zero on a row where the numerator is not. CEL divides to a signed Infinity and IEEE-754 keeps the sign of the zero; SQL cannot tell -0.0 from 0.0, and a NULLIF guard collapses both to NULL. The sign of the Infinity decides which side of an order comparison the row falls on, so no guard recovers it and the adapter refuses. A constant denominator, or a column divided by itself, stays translatable

arithmetic/divide/int-by-list-index.reason: Index into a literal list: only a relation mapped with order_field, or a map literal keyed by a string attribute, is translated.

arithmetic/divide/int-by-ternary.reason: The translator divides an int() result only by an operand it knows is an int; a ternary's numeric type is not carried by the plan, so the division is refused.

arithmetic/divide/negated-int-by-ternary.reason: The translator divides an int() result only by an operand it knows is an int; a ternary's numeric type is not carried by the plan, so the division is refused.

arithmetic/divide/nested-division-diviso.reason: The inner divisor is a column that may be zero; SQL cannot preserve the IEEE signed-zero infinity needed to evaluate the nested division.

cast/double/malformed-string.reason: SQL CAST reads a string's leading digits where CEL double() rejects the whole string; double() over a string column is refused.

cast/double/negated-malformed-string.reason: SQL floating-point casts accept malformed string prefixes or coerce them to zero, unlike CEL errors; negation cannot make the conversion safe.

cast/string/from-integral-ternary.reason: string() over a ternary of whole-number constants is refused: the plan carries 1000000 and 1000000.0 as the same number, and CEL spells the int "1000000" and the double "1e+06", so SQL cannot know which text to produce.

cast/string/from-negative-zero-double.reason: string() over a double column is compared by reading the literal back as the double CEL spells that way; "-0" is -0.0, and SQL (SQLite's REAL, PostgreSQL's and MySQL's DOUBLE) compares -0.0 equal to 0.0, so the filter could not tell i5 from a row holding 0.0. A zero literal is refused

cast/string/negated-from-integral-ternar.reason: Same untyped whole-number ternary under string() as cast/string/from-integral-ternary, under negation.

cast/timestamp/malformed-string.reason: timestamp() over a column holding a formatted string would compare text in SQL, not instants; the attribute must map to a datetime column.

cast/timestamp/negated-malformed-string.reason: The mapper supplies a string column; the adapter only compares instants through native temporal columns, without portable error-preserving parsing of malformed strings.

collection/exists/map-keys.reason: exists() over the parent ranges over the keys of a map, and the parent is a to-one association, which the adapter refuses as a macro's collection: a subquery over it ranges over rows, and SQL has no way to enumerate which of a row's columns are non-NULL as the map's keys.

collection/exists/negated-map-keys.reason: Same to-one parent read as a map as collection/exists/map-keys, under negation.

collection/exists/two-variable-map-key-a.reason: A two-variable exists() over a map binds each key beside its value. obj is not a stored map but columns of the resource row, and SQL cannot enumerate a row's columns as keys, so the second variable has nothing to bind to. Over a relation with order_field the position binds; over a map it is refused.

comparison/equals/list-holding-nan.reason: `==` with a list built from a computed element (`aDouble / 0.0`) is refused: only eq and ne against constant lists are translated.

membership/in/map-attribute-keys.reason: in over the parent tests the keys of a map, and the parent is a to-one association, which the adapter refuses as a membership haystack: an EXISTS over it tests rows, and SQL has no way to enumerate which of a row's columns are non-NULL as the map's keys.

membership/in/negated-map-attribute-keys.reason: Same to-one parent read as a map as membership/in/map-attribute-keys, under negation.

regex/matches/case-insensitive-non-ascii.reason: The RE2 lowering expands (?i) through a table of ASCII and known Unicode folding orbits; É is not tabulated, so the pattern is refused rather than folded by a store collation that is not RE2's.

regex/matches/dot-all-flag.reason: The RE2 lowering reads only a leading (?i) and (?:...) groups; (?s), under which . also matches a newline, is refused.

regex/matches/end-anchor-mid-pattern.reason: The RE2 lowering reads ^ and $ only at the ends of the pattern or of a top-level branch; an anchor followed by more pattern is refused.

regex/matches/field-to-field.reason: matches() is lowered only for a constant pattern, which is parsed as RE2 before translation; a pattern read from a row would reach the database's own regex dialect, which is not RE2.

regex/matches/negated-class.reason: A negated character class matches an unbounded set of characters, which the lowering to literals and LIKE cannot enumerate, so the pattern is refused.

regex/matches/non-digit-class.reason: The RE2 lowering does not read \D, an unbounded class it cannot enumerate, so the pattern is refused.

regex/matches/two-dot-star-gaps.reason: Two .* gaps are not a finite set of literals or a single prefix-and-suffix LIKE, and LIKE's % would cross a newline RE2's . does not, so the pattern is refused.

regex/matches/unanchored-dot.reason: A . between two literals is not a finite set of literals, and LIKE's _ would match a newline RE2's . does not, so the pattern is refused.

regex/matches/word-boundary.reason: The RE2 lowering does not read \b, which has no LIKE equivalent, so the pattern is refused.

size/greater-than/map-projection.reason: size() of a map() projection: each element is read through the lambda body, and a body that errors on one element (b6's unnamed tag) makes the whole count an error. The adapter counts only a named collection or a filter(), so the projection is refused.

timestamp/equals/field-to-field-without-.reason: SQL temporal columns preserve instants but discard the RFC-3339 spelling compared by bare CEL attributes; timestamp wrappers are required.
